decisions.reason: The encrypted second channel is central to the firm's announced direction toward binding mobile communication and trusted second-channel interactions, so the visible commitment and sunk R&D make keeping it likely.
The mobile PDF signature supports the announced push into online contract signing, and early weak results can still be blamed on slow market adoption, so management will persist with it.

The multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is a core platform investment that frames the firm's whole offering, so dropping it would write off substantial R&D and contradict the firm's public positioning.
The email-to-app delivery robot is a narrower add-on, but it fits the secure-communication ecosystem the firm has announced, and its first-year results can still be read as a temporary adoption lag.

The QR-code hardware token involves hardware investment and serves regulated customers, so despite a move toward app-based approaches the firm will likely keep it rather than expose the earlier decision as a mistake.
The payment network compliance suite matches the firm's regulatory-security claims, and after only one year any disappointing uptake is attributable to temporary causes, so management keeps it.
